title: PosePlaner: Denoising Any Feedforward Pose Predictor from Pairwise Planar Geometry
claim: A plug-in refiner takes drifting feed-forward estimates and, using geometric correspondences, outputs corrected estimates that match ground truth.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, center zoom-in callouts, bottom stage labels with arrows
description: The figure reads left to right as input, refiner, output. On the left, a wobbly blue camera trajectory with blue frustums drifts away from a black ground-truth trajectory. Five small indoor photos sit beside it, and two of them are enlarged with grid overlays, outlined in green and orange. The middle has two rounded callout boxes. The upper box, 'Cross-view 3D Plane Correspondences', shows green and orange polygons linked by dashed arrows. A hollow arrow leads down to the lower box, 'Plane-Embedded Diffusion'. That box shows a blue camera icon labelled T_init, a pink graph network, and a red camera icon labelled T_refine, with the update equation underneath. A hollow arrow leads to the right panel. There, the red refined trajectory lies close to the black ground truth, and faded blue shows the original drift. Bottom labels read Input, Diffusion Refiner and Output, joined by gray arrows.
caption: Our proposed PosePlaner refines any feed-forward pose in one Euler step of a plane-embedded diffusion adapter, and extends to $n$-view streaming via per-edge view-graph refinement aggregated by rotation averaging and a Glomap-style positioner. Left: $T_{init}$ (blue) drifts from GT (black). Middle: conditioned on per-view planar primitives, the refiner yields $T_{refine} = T_{init}\cdot\Delta T_\theta(T_{init}\midplanes)$ (red) in one step. Right: refined trajectory (red), raw feed-forward (blue), GT (black).
abstract: Recent multi-view Transformers (e.g., DUSt3R and VGGT) have advanced 3D reconstruction by scaling training data and model capacity from two views to many views and long sequences, subsuming the classical SfM/SLAM pipeline of feature extraction, matching, and pose estimation in a single feed-forward pass. Yet this subsumption hides the interfaces between pipeline stages---correspondences, geometry, and pose are entangled in a single forward pass, leaving supervised fine-tuning as the major path to improvement and offering no mechanism to correct predictions from geometric evidence at test time. We propose PosePlaner to close this gap by reviving the classical coupling between correspondences and pose via flow matching, treating pose refinement as a conditional generation problem that takes coarse geometric matches and initial pose as input condition and fuses the resulting pose hypotheses into a single refined estimate, providing a continuous, data-driven analog of RANSAC voting. Our method is trained efficiently on two-view data, yet serves as a periodic refiner for streaming n-view pose estimators with no retraining. Empirically, it corrects failures of feed-forward predictors, substantially improves correspondence-based solvers, and reduces accumulated drift in long streaming sequences.
